sections.heading: Carried by more than one source

items.title: GitHub Actions leaking secrets when Miri output is cached
items.blurb: The Rust Security Response Team was notified that Miri stores all environment variables to target/ , allowing secrets to persist in caches.

items.title: Be alert: targeted attacks on prominent Rustaceans
items.blurb: We believe that there is an ongoing campaign targeting rust-lang members and owners of popular crates that is attempting to compromise devices and accounts in order to use them to publish malware.

items.title: Saving another 100TB of RAM with math (and Rust)
items.blurb: Cloudflare's global network is immense but not limitless. As we look for small ways to trim our resource usage, we sometimes get lucky and we can cut significantly more.

items.title: Adversarial examples for fast hash functions
items.blurb: AI discovered collisions in komihash, a5hash, HighwayHash, SpookyHash, aHash, and t1ha2! It also includes the standard hashes in Rust, Go, and .NET. submitted by /u/thomasahle [link] [comments]

items.title: Announcing a Maintainer in Residence: Scott Schafer for the Cargo team
items.blurb: At the end of August, we announced our first Maintainers in Residence, Rust Project contributors who are funded for their upstream contributions and maintenance work from the Rust Foundation Maintainers Fund (RFMF).

items.title: Home Made CobbleDB Replaces DynamoDB at Perplexity to Cut Query Latency 5x and Reduce Cloud Storage
items.blurb: Perplexity has migrated its search infrastructure from Amazon DynamoDB to CobbleDB, an internally developed key-value store in Rust. This change reduced latency and costs associated with handling large document batches.

items.title: Rust debugging survey 2026 results
items.blurb: One of the biggest challenges Rust developers report in our annual surveys is a subpar debugging experience.

items.title: Cloudflare Cuts 100 TB of Memory from 1.1.1.1 DNS Cache
items.blurb: Cloudflare redesigned the in-memory representation of its Big Pineapple DNS cache, reducing the per-entry footprint by 56% and freeing roughly 100 TB of working-set memory across its fleet.
